rejected.title: Coenzymes
card: A coenzyme is a small organic molecule that is not a protein. It helps an enzyme by carrying energy, electrons or hydrogen from one reaction to another.
ATP
carries energy. When ATP loses a phosphate it becomes ADP, and the energy released powers other reactions. ADP is later recharged to ATP.
NADH
the loaded form of NAD+. It picks up electrons and hydrogen in reactions that break down food, such as cellular respiration, and unloads to NAD+.
NADPH
the loaded form of NADP+. It delivers electrons and hydrogen to reactions that build molecules, such as making sugar in photosynthesis, and becomes NADP+ again.
rejected.remember: Coenzymes cycle between loaded and unloaded forms. NADH works in breakdown reactions, NADPH in building ones.

a.q: Which coenzyme mainly carries energy for use in other cell reactions?
a.why: ATP carries energy, which is released when it loses a phosphate and becomes ADP. ADP is tempting, but it is the unloaded form that must be recharged before it can carry energy again.
a.clue: Which form still has its energy to give?

b.q: A chloroplast is building sugar. Which coenzyme supplies the electrons and hydrogen, and what form does it end up as?
opts: NADPH, which ends up as NADP+
NADH, which ends up as NAD+
ATP, which ends up as ADP
NADP+, which ends up as NADPH
b.why: NADPH delivers electrons and hydrogen to building reactions such as making sugar, and unloads to NADP+. NADH is tempting, but it works in breakdown reactions like respiration. NADP+ is the unloaded form, so it has nothing to supply.
b.clue: Is this reaction building or breaking down, and which form is loaded?

draft.title: Coenzymes
card: A coenzyme is a small molecule that helps an enzyme by carrying something between reactions. It is not a protein enzyme itself.
ATP
carries energy. Energy is released when ATP is broken down, and this energy powers other reactions in the cell.
NADH
carries electrons and hydrogen from one reaction to another, such as those that release energy from food.
NADPH
also carries electrons and hydrogen. Cells use it to supply them to reactions that build molecules, such as sugars in photosynthesis.
draft.remember: Coenzymes such as ATP, NADH and NADPH carry energy, electrons or hydrogen between reactions.

a.q: Which coenzyme mainly carries energy for use in other cell reactions?
a.why: ATP carries energy that is released when it is broken down. NADH is tempting, but it carries electrons and hydrogen.
a.clue: Think about which one is broken down to release energy.

b.q: A cell needs to deliver electrons and hydrogen to a reaction that builds sugar. Which coenzyme is used?
b.why: NADPH carries electrons and hydrogen to reactions that build molecules. ATP carries energy rather than electrons and hydrogen.
b.clue: Which carrier moves electrons and hydrogen for building reactions?

problems.detail: Two of the four options, Amylase (an enzyme) and Water, are plainly not coenzymes. That leaves a choice between ATP and NADPH, which the question's own wording ('electrons and hydrogen', 'builds sugar') settles directly. This is too easy for Year 12.

check.summary: The facts are correct and the intended answers (ATP, NADPH) are right. Question b is very easy because two of its distractors are not coenzymes at all.
